analysis:
Examined workflow metadata, the complete supplied patch, and both BASE source excerpts. .github/workflows/ci.yml head lines 43–47 replace one five-runner provider lane with five one-runner lanes; head line 142 selects the lane using the existing numeric shard matrix. All five names match the BASE matrix values (lines 140–141). This permits partial Sandbox allocation with remaining shards using the existing Blacksmith fallback, rather than whole-group fallback.
No concrete security regression is established. Event triggers, read-only contents permission, route job's empty permissions, checkout pins, test prerequisites, suite-count auditing, artifact naming, and final fail-closed provider gate are unchanged (BASE lines 3–10, 35–36, 143–150, 358–369, 762–782). No supplied change alters production authorization, attestation, encryption, billing, fan authority, installer execution, or cache confidentiality controls, including T-041. CI execution on Sandbox runners was already supported; this is not evidence of a newly introduced untrusted-runner boundary or credential exposure.
Integration should check the directly consumed .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml contract: independent named lanes must preserve runner/lease isolation and return every requested key, including fallback keys. Its implementation is not supplied, so neither correct allocation nor a missing isolation control can be established here. Mixed-runner builds also continue through the existing provider-ci-build action and summary audit; no cache or artifact bypass is visible in this workflow. Remaining uncertainty concerns the routing contract, not a demonstrated vulnerability or production qualification claim.
